A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, theoretical framework and main experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including retained Appendices A–C and v2's added Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on COPYFIRST, COPYLAST, ROCKETMAN and three real-world forecasting datasets, including Table 1 and Figures 3, 4 and 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original EngRAD rewiring results in Table 2 and temporal tree feature-matching results in Appendix D, Table 5.

M1.justification: The factorized MPTCN architecture, TTS/T&S formulations and temporal rewiring mechanisms remain unchanged. Section 5.1 adds evaluated adaptations using FOSR spatial rewiring and an RGCN alternative to DCNN that weights rewired edges differently.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds TEMPORALTREENEIGHBOURSMATCH, a classification task routing a matching sender's label through a tree, with features active at the first or last time step. Existing synthetic and real-world datasets remain. ROCKETMAN's appearance by name in the main text is not new coverage; v1 already documented it in Appendix B.

E2.justification: The new EngRAD comparison evaluates FOSR-rewired DCNN and RGCN variants against the original graph configuration, with standard and normalized temporal convolutions. FOSR was previously cited but not evaluated. Table 1 retains the same MPTCN and original/TTS Graph WaveNet comparators.

E3.justification: The added tree experiment fixes T = 4, varies tree depth across 3, 4 and 5, contrasts first versus last active time steps, and reports classification accuracy. Table 2 introduces a controlled rewiring comparison in the TTS setting. Previously documented splits, preprocessing, training budgets and forecasting metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an EngRAD ablation separating spatial rewiring, temporal normalization and their combination, including the DCNN/RGCN choice. Appendix D adds a diagnostic of tree depth and feature timing. These supplement the retained depth, kernel-size and topology analyses with checks of combined mitigation and spatially dominated failure.

E5.justification: Both versions report success rates across unspecified multiple runs and numerical results with ± values. The added tables follow this existing reporting practice; v2 supplies no new run counts, seed information, definitions of the uncertainty terms, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 scores and matched experimental plots are unchanged. New Table 2 reports EngRAD MAE of 40.30±0.16 for normalized FOSR/DCNN and 41.10±0.11 for normalized FOSR/RGCN, alongside the retained unrewired value 40.38±0.08. New Table 5 reports depth-4 accuracy of 1.00±0.00 for first-step features versus 0.73±0.46 for last-step features. These are additional configurations and tasks.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, Proposition 4.2, the appendix assumptions and proofs, and the computational-complexity derivations are retained. Index cleanups and the new matrix-power illustration in Figure 5 do not introduce or revise mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: characterizing spatiotemporal over-squashing, identifying the temporal bias of causal convolutions, and establishing matching sensitivity bounds for TTS and T&S under fixed budgets. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains the temporal bias through propagation paths and self-loops, qualifies TTS applicability to changing graph topologies, and notes limited normalization benefits for intermediate-time readouts. It adds the conservative worst-case-bound limitation and interprets the new tree experiment as primarily spatially bottlenecked, limiting its diagnostic usefulness.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly provides a repository link for reproducing the experiments. Existing hardware, software, training-time and implementation disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Bamberger et al. on measuring long-range interactions, Schlichtkrull et al. for RGCN, and Gravina et al. on continuous-time dynamic graphs. Related work briefly distinguishes that dynamic-graph research while retaining the original novelty positioning. Other reference changes largely concern metadata or numbering.

P1.justification: v2 organizes empirical validation into Section 5.1 with descriptive subheadings, expands the temporal mechanism explanation and limitations, and adds Appendix D. Local wording and conference-header edits accompany these additions; most existing prose and the overall argument structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains information-flow diagrams and a fuller caption; Figure 3 changes from vertically stacked to horizontal panels. v2 adds sensitivity curves in Figure 5 and results Tables 2 and 5. Existing ROCKETMAN figures, dataset statistics and complexity tables are retained with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the joint-rewiring ablation in Table 2 and complementary classification experiment in Appendix D strengthen empirical support, while clearer diagrams, specific applicability limits and a reproduction-code link improve explanation and transparency. The core theory and previous results remain intact. Limited protocol detail and unspecified uncertainty reporting constrain the new evidence, so the overall improvement is modest.
